contrary_evidence: September BRICS declaration describes interoperability and local-currency payments, not an adopted common currency.
Domestic Pix scale does not quantify dollar displacement or foregone foreign card-network fees.
DFC financing and Serra Verde ownership/offtake agreements predate the October presidential runoff and Flávio's departure.
US reported current non-recognition posture on 30 October weakens an assertion of immediate alternative-president sponsorship.
No reviewed negotiating document establishes a conditional exchange of US admission for Brazilian minerals or Pix concessions.
limitations: USGS rare-earth reserve estimates and 2025 production are vintage-specific statistical measures; May 2026 revision replaced an earlier Brazil estimate.
SPV financing commitments and forward purchases do not imply all US$1.55bn was paid out to the mine; future debt funding remains conditional.
Company-stated ramp-up capacities and projected downstream production are not independently verified achieved output.
Official BCB headline Pix statistics reflect domestic activity and cannot measure international payment substitution.
Migration status and confidential bilateral negotiating correspondence are not fully public; alleged cross-issue conditionality remains unproven.
Strict full-draft depth workflow retains five previously rejected older drafts; production CI passed candidate-relevant gates. Full local clone unavailable.

contrary_evidence: The official September 2026 BRICS declaration prioritizes interoperability and local currencies, not a single monetary authority.
Pix September 2026 domestic volume does not quantify the diversion of Visa/Mastercard revenue or dollar settlement.
The US-Brazil trade working group and documented minerals interest predate the October election and Flávio's departure.
US statements on 30 October indicate no current plan to recognize Flávio as Brazilian president.
Brazil formally contests the USTR Section 301 assessment; the US allegations remain attributed positions.
There is no documentary proof in the reviewed source set of an explicit protection-for-minerals or Pix concession exchange.
The prior MCS2026 Brazil rare earth reserve value of 21 million tonnes REO was revised in May 2026 to 11 million; the latest value is used in both charts and references.

Serra Verde's completed September USA Rare Earth takeover and 15-year US-backed offtake predate the October Brazilian election; they establish real ownership/contractual control but not a migration-for-minerals exchange.
